findings.description: verify_project_access accepts require_write=True but only enforces it for non-LEAD developers. CEOs, PMs, and LEADs always have write access regardless of the flag. The authorization model doesn't distinguish between read and write project permissions for most roles.

Traceability endpoints trust the project_id field in PR documents without validating that the PR's repository actually belongs to that project. A malicious or incorrect project_id could allow access to PRs from inaccessible projects.
Method signature changed to require current_user parameter. Existing callers that don't pass it will break with TypeError at runtime.

findings.issue: File history endpoint uses has_org_access instead of project verification
findings.description: The get_file_history endpoint requires org access instead of project-scoped access. A DEVELOPER assigned to a project cannot view file history for that project's repository.

findings.issue: Entity connections endpoint doesn't verify access to all entity types
findings.description: The get_entity_connections endpoint verifies access for TASK and PR entity types but skips authorization for other types (FILE, COMMIT, DEPLOYMENT, etc.), exposing those connections without access control.

findings.issue: Recommendations entity endpoint doesn't verify PR access
findings.description: The get_entity_recommendations endpoint only checks has_org_access for PRs without verifying the PR belongs to an accessible project. A DEVELOPER could list recommendations for PRs from inaccessible projects.
